clue.text: The guy I call out is spiralling

parts.note: the guy is simply 'he'

indicators.note: a call that is out has been thrown off its usual course, so its letters are set in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone describes a man as being in a downward spiral after a phone call goes out.
explanation.definitionFit: Helical means shaped like a helix, a coil or corkscrew, which is what a spiralling thing traces.

clue.text: This is why we hear unorthodox view

parts.note: 'here's' is a way of presenting 'this is'

indicators.note: what we hear is a word's sound rather than its spelling, so the question word is taken by how it is said

parts.note: the question word is said exactly like the letter Y

explanation.surface: A sentence that seems to be introducing someone's explanation of a dissenting opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: Heresy is a belief contrary to accepted doctrine, an opinion that departs from orthodoxy.

clue.text: Uniform consignment with half the shop gone

indicators.note: something gone has been taken away, so these letters are removed from the longer word

parts.note: a consignment of goods is a delivery
a deli is a shop; half of its four letters is its first two

explanation.surface: A delivery of uniforms arrives, but half the shop has vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: A deli is a delicatessen; dropping its first half from the front of the delivery word leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Livery is the distinctive uniform worn by servants or staff of a company or guild.

clue.text: Suspect carton starting to burst with illegal stuff

indicators.note: used as an adjective, suspect means dodgy or not right, so the carton's letters are out of order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: the start of the next word means only its opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of the word
'and' joins things together just as 'with' does

explanation.surface: A dodgy box at customs is about to split open, spilling smuggled goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Contraband is goods imported or exported illegally, smuggled merchandise.

clue.text: Grasshopper mostly in position

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a locust is a kind of grasshopper

explanation.surface: A grasshopper sits mostly still, in its spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A locus is a particular place or position, as in the locus of a crime or a point in geometry.

clue.text: Cleopatra cheated a bit and got it in the neck

indicators.note: a bit is only a part, so the answer is a stretch of the words before it

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the end of the queen's name and the start of the verb

explanation.surface: Cleopatra played a little foul and was punished for it, perhaps by the asp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got it in the neck' is an idiom for being severely punished; here 'it in the neck' is read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The trachea is the windpipe, the tube running down the front of the neck.

clue.text: Top star with rogue nation director

indicators.note: to top something is to cut off its head, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: taken as written before its head is cut

indicators.note: a rogue state behaves out of line, so the letters of nation are disordered

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A leading actor teams up with a filmmaker from a rogue state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top star' looks like a famous name, but 'Top' is a verb meaning behead.
explanation.definitionFit: Quentin Tarantino is the American film director of Pulp Fiction and Kill Bill.

clue.text: See 23
Dry death foiled by being this

definitions.text: Dry death foiled by being this

indicators.note: a foiled plan is thwarted and knocked off course, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Death by dehydration is prevented if one stays in this state.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the anagram of the first two words is the state that prevents them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well supplied with water is exactly what stops someone dying of thirst.

clue.text: After foolish day, financial centre gets winter warmth

parts.note: April Fools' Day is 1 April, written APR I with the abbreviated month and the Roman numeral
the City is London's financial district

explanation.surface: After April Fools' Day, the financial world enjoys a spell of mild weather.
explanation.walkthrough: The City of London is the capital's banking district, so 'financial centre' gives CITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Apricity is a rare word for the warmth of the sun on a cold winter's day.

clue.text: Hell-bent, without divorcing at first, to get separated

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: someone hell-bent on a goal is driven

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the preceding word only

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A determined couple, not divorced at first, end up split apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Riven is the past participle of rive, to tear or split apart.

clue.text: My dear, in cooking find a herb

parts.note: both are exclamations of surprise

indicators.note: cooking mixes ingredients up, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook addresses a loved one while hunting for a herb in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My dear' reads as a term of endearment, but 'My' is an exclamation like 'Cor!', British slang for surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Coriander is a herb whose leaves and seeds are used widely in cooking.

clue.text: Unpredictable ending of talks with rebel leader in revolt

indicators.note: the ending of a word means only its last letter is wanted

parts.note: the last letter of the word

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a revolt is an uprising

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the one at its front

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Peace talks end badly when a rebel commander takes part in an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: The rebel's initial goes after the first letter of the uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Something surprising is unexpected, so it could not have been predicted.

clue.text: To begin with, take a little curry powder

indicators.note: to begin with means using only the beginning of each word that follows

parts.note: the first letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: start by adding a pinch of curry powder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curry powder' looks like one phrase, but the last word is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc is a soft mineral ground into talcum powder for the skin.

clue.text: Water creature starting to twitch indeed, lacking water

indicators.note: read as two words, in deed, the first word puts the earlier pieces inside the second

parts.note: the second half of the word, read as in deed

indicators.note: the start of the next word means only its opening letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
the Hydra was a many-headed water serpent of Greek myth

explanation.surface: A water creature twitches at the start, truly short of moisture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indeed' splits into 'in deed': the creature and the T go inside DEED, making DE-HYDRAT-ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Dehydrated means having lost or been deprived of water.

clue.text: Fighting soldier's back to be embraced by beautiful woman, with tears

indicators.note: something embraced is held inside, so it sits within the other word

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman

indicators.note: going back means reading the soldier's letters from the end

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
rent as in rips, the verb tears

explanation.surface: A soldier is hugged by a lovely woman and both weep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tears' looks like crying, but it means rips, giving RENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Belligerent describes a party engaged in war, or someone aggressive and hostile.

clue.text: A European tucking into refined meal that's light

indicators.note: tucking into means going inside, so these pieces are placed within the other
something refined has been processed and reworked, so the meal's letters are reordered

parts.note: a Serb is a European from Serbia
taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A European diner eats a dainty meal that is not heavy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' looks like a description of the meal, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser beam is a narrow, intense beam of light.

clue.text: Ignoring the odds, profane 4 can be derisive

indicators.note: can be suggests what the letters might turn into, so they are rearranged
ignoring the odd-numbered letters leaves only the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: the even letters of the word
the answer to 4 down

explanation.surface: Swearing about long odds can come across as mocking.
explanation.walkthrough: The 4 is a cross-reference to the 4 down answer, whose letters join the even letters of 'profane' in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Scornful means showing contempt, the same sneering attitude as derisive.

clue.text: Show approval for role reversal nonsense

parts.note: to clap is to show approval

indicators.note: the word reversal itself tells us to read the role backwards

parts.note: an actor's role is a part

explanation.surface: Applauding an actor who swaps roles seems like rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is pretentious or empty talk, a synonym of rubbish.

clue.text: Medical procedure: very backwards and not original

parts.note: the punctuation mark itself is called a colon

indicators.note: backwards means the word is read from its end to its start

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
a copy is not an original

explanation.surface: A doctor describing an operation that is hardly original and done in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon in the clue is part of the wordplay, and neatly also names the organ examined.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonoscopy is an examination of the large intestine with a camera on a flexible tube.

clue.text: Vile musical abandoned by a Spice Girl

indicators.note: being abandoned by someone means they leave, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: melodious means tuneful or musical
Mel B and Mel C were both in the Spice Girls

explanation.surface: A dreadful stage show is deserted by one of the 1990s pop group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'musical' looks like a noun, a stage show, but it is the adjective, tuneful.
explanation.definitionFit: Odious means hateful or repugnant, much like vile.

clue.text: Areas dealing with charity

parts.note: re means concerning or regarding
alms are charitable gifts to the poor

explanation.surface: Fields of work concerned with charitable giving.
explanation.definitionFit: Realms are domains or fields, areas of activity or territory.

clue.text: Delighted in a blanket, by the sound of it

indicators.note: going by the sound means we hear a word and spell it differently

parts.note: someone in a blanket is wrapped up

explanation.surface: Someone is thrilled to be snuggled under a blanket.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapt means completely absorbed or enraptured, filled with delight.

clue.text: Perhaps one-all game of defence

parts.note: a one-all scoreline is an example of a draw
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A tied score in a match decided by defensive play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks one-all as just one example of a draw.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawbridge is a castle's raising bridge across a moat, part of its defences.

clue.text: Drinking tea used to be method to lose weight

indicators.note: something drinking takes a liquid inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: was is the past of 'to be'
taken as written
a way of doing something is a method

explanation.surface: A dieter claims drinking tea was their way to slim down.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb 'used to be' and 'method' sit either side of the tea, which goes inside them: WAS-TEA-WAY.
explanation.definitionFit: To waste away is to grow thin and weak, losing weight through illness.

clue.text: Essentially bypassed quiet bay to reach land

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only the central letters are kept

parts.note: the two central letters of the eight-letter word
the central letter of the word
the central letter of the word

explanation.surface: A ship skirts a calm bay on its voyage to reach a continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the largest continent, a land mass.

clue.text: Woodworkers in favour of organic compounds

parts.note: to be for something is to favour it
esters are a class of organic chemical compounds

explanation.surface: Carpenters back the use of natural chemicals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woodworkers' suggests carpenters, but it means people who work in woods.
explanation.definitionFit: Foresters manage and work in forests, so they are workers among the woods.

clue.text: Gruff hazard for undesirable poster

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the monster under the bridge in the tale of the Three Billy Goats Gruff
second meaning: someone who posts provocative messages online

explanation.surface: A grumpy danger to an unwanted placard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gruff' looks like an adjective, but it is the goats' name from the folk tale.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the fairy-tale bridge monster and an internet provocateur who posts to cause trouble.

clue.text: It's soothing to find one empty pub in a restored mall

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the earlier pieces go within the other
something restored has been reworked, so the letters of mall are rebuilt in a new order
an empty word has lost its insides, leaving just its outer letters

parts.note: the outer letters of the word
taken as written, to be rearranged
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A relaxing drink in a deserted pub inside a refurbished shopping centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip balm is a waxy ointment that soothes dry or chapped lips; 'It's soothing' describes the product.

clue.text: Discarding the cover to fix disc? Yes!

indicators.note: to fix something is to rework it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone removes a protective case to repair a disc, with a triumphant yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecdysis is moulting, the shedding of an outer skin or shell by insects and reptiles.
